CIRCDIST.gross#candidate-certification.i.text: Via SBB26 Thm 1 the statement d_circ = 11 for the candidate circuit reduces to an exact minimum-distance certification on a 360-column extended code (not a circuit-level DEM search); combined with the universal d_ext cap this certifies the first half of the claim and pins the achievable floor at 11.

CIRCDIST.gross#gap-via-lift.implication.text: Given the universal d_ext <= 11 cap, D* = 12 holds iff some interleaved schedule has completion gap >= 1 at weight 12; the closed-lift criterion turns this into a voltage/monodromy condition checkable per witness family, deciding the second half of the claim in either direction.

CIRCDIST.gross.claim.text: For the Gross code [[144,12,12]] with single-ancilla CNOT syndrome extraction (interleaving of X- and Z-check CNOTs allowed; each required CNOT exactly once; one two-qubit gate per qubit per time step; no flag ancillas, cat states, or generating-set changes; idle layers compressed), the optimum D*_Gross = max over legal schedules M of d_circ(C(M)) is determined with proof, as either an explicit interleaved schedule with certified d_circ = 12, or a proof that every legal schedule satisfies d_circ <= 11; and the published conjectured distance-11 circuit has a certified d_circ = 11.

CIRCDIST.gross.dext-cap.claim.text: For the Gross code [[144,12,12]], every legal single-ancilla CNOT syndrome-extraction schedule M — interleaved or not — satisfies d_ext(E(M)) <= 11.

CIRCDIST.lift.iff.claim.text: In graph-like detector error models with fixed boundaries, for memory experiments C_R(M) with R >= d_sec (the spatial distance of the sector's own logical class: d_X for the Z-memory, d_Z for the X-memory), d_circ equals the minimum over nontrivial effective logicals gamma of the length of the shortest closed spacetime lift of gamma, with an intrinsic zero-voltage/monodromy condition characterizing same-weight liftability at minimum weight — and the voltage is computable without constructing the full multi-round circuit (non-vacuity bar).
